summary: Requests that RFC 1745, BGP4/IDRP for IP---OSPF Interaction, be moved to Historic status because the technology was never deployed in the public internet.

plainLanguage.summary: This memo asks to move RFC 1745 to Historic status. It says the BGP4/IDRP and OSPF interaction was never deployed in the public Internet.

questions: why was bgp4 idrp ospf never deployed
why does rfc 3167 request historic status
what was the rfc 1745 routing interaction
subtitle: Requests Historic status for the BGP4/IDRP and OSPF interaction described in RFC 1745.

tldr.problem: RFC 1745 described a BGP4/IDRP-OSPF interaction that the memo says was never deployed in the public Internet.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 3167 requests moving RFC 1745 to Historic status because of non-deployment and implementation complexity.
tldr.outcome: The memo documents a request to retire the specification's active status and says the change has no known security effect.

today: RFC 3167 is an Informational memo requesting Historic status for RFC 1745.

sections.title: The RFC 1745 Interaction
sections.content:
RFC 1745 describes interaction among BGP4, IDRP, and OSPF for IP. RFC 3167 says this mechanism was never deployed in the public Internet.

The memo states that implementation would require significant complexity. It provides a short rationale for reclassifying the earlier RFC.
sections.plainLanguage: The earlier RFC described a way for routing systems to interact. The later memo reports that the approach was never deployed publicly.

sections.title: Why Historic Status Is Requested
sections.content:
RFC 3167 proposes Historic status because the mechanism had never been used in the public Internet and would be complex to implement.

The document does not specify a replacement. It says moving RFC 1745 to Historic has no known effect on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo argues there is no reason to keep the unused, complex design as active guidance. It does not propose a new routing design.

sections.title: Reference and Scope
sections.content:
The memo cites RFC 1745, “BGP4/IDRP for IP—OSPF Interaction,” published in December 1994. RFC 3167 is a status request, not a protocol specification.

Its scope is the proposed reclassification of RFC 1745. The security section states that the status move has no known effect on Internet security.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo only addresses the status of RFC 1745. It does not change the behavior of BGP4, IDRP, or OSPF.

references.text: Varadhan, K., Hares, S. and Y. Rekhter, "BGP4/IDRP for IP---OSPF Interaction", RFC 1745, December 1994.
